## 1. Execution attempts

Every job admitted to Orion is executed by a worker. An execution attempt is one delivery of the job to a worker that either succeeds, fails, or times out. Orion bounds the number of attempts so that a job that cannot succeed does not consume worker capacity forever.

Normative rule
1. A job must be executed at most three times in total.
2. The first execution counts as one of the three.
3. When the third execution has ended without success, no further execution of that job may be started.

Example
A job whose first two executions fail is executed a third time. If that execution also fails, the job has exhausted its attempts.

## 2. Retry delay

After an execution attempt fails, Orion waits before delivering the job again. The wait gives transient downstream faults time to clear without hammering the dependency that just failed.

Normative rule
1. Before every retry attempt the worker must wait exactly five seconds, measured from the end of the failed attempt.
2. The wait must not be shortened or lengthened based on the attempt number.

Example
An attempt fails at 10:00:00. The next attempt may start no earlier than 10:00:05. If that attempt also fails at 10:00:20, the following attempt may start no earlier than 10:00:25.

## 3. Attempt timeout

A worker that hangs must not hold a job indefinitely. Each attempt is bounded by a timeout after which the attempt is treated as failed and the retry policy applies.

Normative rule
1. Each execution attempt must time out after thirty seconds of execution.
2. An attempt that reaches the timeout must be recorded as a failed attempt.

Example
An attempt starts at 12:00:00 and has not completed by 12:00:30. Orion records the attempt as failed at 12:00:30.

## 4. Duplicate delivery

Producers may deliver the same job more than once, for example after a network timeout on the producer side. Orion must not execute a job twice because of such redelivery.

Normative rule
1. While a job with a given job id is active, any further delivery carrying the same job id must be ignored.
2. Ignoring a duplicate delivery must not change the state of the active job.

Example
Job J-17 is delivered at 09:00 and is executing. A second delivery of J-17 arrives at 09:01 and is ignored; J-17 continues unaffected.

## 5. Idempotency keys

Each delivery may carry an idempotency key chosen by the producer. Orion remembers keys for a bounded period so that repeated deliveries with the same key can be recognised.

Normative rule
1. Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen.
2. After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.

Example
Key K-9 is first seen on Monday at 08:00. A delivery with K-9 on Monday at 20:00 is recognised as a repeat. A delivery with K-9 on Tuesday at 09:00 is treated as new.

## 6. Worker lease

A worker that receives a job holds a lease on it. The lease is how Orion knows that the job is being worked on and prevents a second worker from taking it.

Normative rule
1. A worker lease must last sixty seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
2. When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.

Example
A worker receives job J-4 at 14:00:00 and neither renews nor releases it. At 14:01:00 the lease expires and J-4 may be delivered to another worker.

## 7. Lease renewal

Long-running work must be able to keep its lease. A worker renews the lease to signal that it is still progressing.

Normative rule
1. A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.
2. A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.

Example
A worker holding a sixty-second lease that started at 14:00:00 renews at 14:00:30; the lease now runs until 14:01:30.

## 8. Cancellation

A producer or operator may cancel a job. Cancellation stops Orion from investing further effort in the job, but Orion does not forcibly abort work that a worker is already performing.

Normative rule
1. After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
2. Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt that is already running; that attempt runs to its own completion, failure or timeout.

Example
Job J-8 is cancelled while its second attempt is running. The second attempt continues; when it ends, no third attempt is started.

## 9. Final failure handling

When a job has used all of its attempts without success, Orion must decide what happens to it. Orion parks such jobs where they can be inspected without blocking the queue.

Normative rule
1. After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
2. A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.

Example
Job J-2 fails its last permitted attempt at 16:05. Orion moves J-2 to the dead-letter queue at 16:05 without operator involvement.

## 10. Operator escalation

Repeated dead-letter events for one tenant usually indicate a systemic fault rather than isolated bad jobs. Orion escalates to an operator when the rate of such events crosses a threshold.

Normative rule
1. When three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within one hour, Orion must raise an operator escalation.
2. The one-hour window must be measured from the first of the three events.

Example
Tenant T-1 accumulates dead-letter events at 10:05, 10:40 and 10:55. The third event is within one hour of the first, so an escalation is raised.

## 11. Queue ordering

Producers sometimes depend on jobs being executed in the order they were enqueued. Orion guarantees ordering only where it can do so without serialising the whole service.

Normative rule
1. First-in-first-out execution order must be guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition.
2. No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.

Example
Jobs J-10 and J-11 are enqueued in that order into partition P-3; J-10 begins execution before J-11. Job J-12 in partition P-4 may begin before or after either.

## 12. Audit retention

Every state transition of a job is recorded as an audit event. Audit events support incident investigation and tenant reporting, and are retained for a bounded period.

Normative rule
1. Audit events must be retained for thirty days after they are recorded.
2. After thirty days an audit event may be deleted.

Example
An audit event recorded on 1 March may be deleted on or after 31 March.

1. Audit events must be retained for thirty days after they are recorded.
2. After thirty days an audit event may be deleted.

Example
An audit event written on 2 June may be removed on or after 2 July.

judgment.rationale: The A-series specs all define a cap on how many times Orion may execute a job, including the initial execution and allowed retries.
The B-series specs all prescribe the wait Orion must impose after a failed execution before starting a retry.
The C-series specs all bound how long a single execution may run and require a timed-out execution to be treated as failed.
The D-series specs all state how Orion treats a further delivery of an already-active job so it is not executed twice.
The E-series specs all require Orion to remember producer idempotency keys for a bounded time after first sighting.
The F-series specs all define how long a worker lease lasts from delivery and that expiry without renewal or release makes the job available again.
The G-series specs all describe when a worker may renew a lease and how a renewal extends the lease.
The H-series specs all define what cancellation does to future attempts, an in-flight attempt, and later a repeated cancellation.
The I-series specs all require an exhausted job to be moved to the dead-letter queue and not executed again unless resubmitted.
The J-series specs all trigger an operator escalation when a tenant accumulates three dead-letter events inside a one-hour window.
The K-series specs all limit first-in-first-out execution order to jobs in the same partition and deny any cross-partition order guarantee.
The L-series specs all require job-state audit events to be kept for a bounded period after recording and allow deletion afterward.

proposal.predicate: duplicate delivery while job is active

value.text: While a job with a given job id is active, any further delivery carrying the same job id must be ignored and must not change the state of the active job.

judgment.rationale: EV-O-D01 and EV-O-D09 require ignoring further deliveries of an active job id without changing that job's state.

proposal.predicate: duplicate delivery while job is active

value.text: While a job is active, a further delivery is ignored only when it carries both the same job id and the same idempotency key; a same job id with a different idempotency key must be rejected as conflicting input and must not change the active job's state.

judgment.rationale: EV-O-D10 ignores a redelivery only when job id and idempotency key both match, and rejects a same job id with a different key as conflicting input.
EV-O-L01 and EV-O-L10 require audit events to be retained for thirty days after they are recorded, after which they may be deleted.
EV-O-C01 requires a thirty-second timeout; EV-O-C10 restates the same half-minute limit at which the execution must be stopped.

value.text: Three dead-letter events for the same tenant within one hour, measured from the first of the three events, require an operator escalation.

judgment.rationale: EV-O-J01 and EV-O-J10 require an operator escalation when three dead-letter events occur for one tenant within one hour of the first event.
EV-O-G01 and EV-O-G10 allow a worker to renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.

value.text: A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.

judgment.rationale: EV-O-G01 and EV-O-G10 require a renewal to extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.
EV-O-E01 and EV-O-E10 require each idempotency key to be retained for twenty-four hours after it is first seen, after which it may be forgotten.

value.text: FIFO execution order is guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition; no ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.

judgment.rationale: EV-O-K01 and EV-O-K10 guarantee first-in-first-out order only within a partition and make no ordering promise across partitions.

value.text: A job must be executed at most three times in total, and the first execution counts as one of the three.

judgment.rationale: EV-O-A01 and EV-O-A02 cap a job at three executions in total, with the first execution counted in that cap.

value.text: One original execution of a job may be followed by no more than three retry executions; after the third retry ends without success the job must not be executed again.

judgment.rationale: EV-O-A03 introduces one initial execution plus up to three retries; EV-O-A06 and EV-O-A10 restate that one original execution may be followed by no more than three retries.
EV-O-F01 and EV-O-F06 require a worker lease to last sixty seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
EV-O-F07 changes the lease to ninety seconds from delivery; EV-O-F10 restates that ninety-second duration.

value.text: After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue; a job there must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.

judgment.rationale: EV-O-I01 and EV-O-I10 require automatic dead-lettering after the last unsuccessful attempt and forbid further execution unless explicitly resubmitted.

proposal.predicate: effect on future and in-flight executions

value.text: After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt may be started; cancellation must not interrupt an already running attempt, which runs to its own completion, failure, or timeout.

judgment.rationale: EV-O-H01 and EV-O-H10 forbid starting further attempts after cancellation and require an in-flight attempt to run to its own end.

value.text: If Orion receives a cancellation for a job that is already cancelled, the job must remain cancelled and the repeated cancellation must not otherwise change the job's state.

judgment.rationale: EV-O-H09 adds that a repeated cancellation leaves an already cancelled job unchanged; EV-O-H10 restates that rule.
EV-O-B01, EV-O-B04, EV-O-B08, and EV-O-B10 require a wait of exactly five seconds before every retry, not varied by attempt number.

value.text: Before the first retry the worker must wait two seconds from the failed execution; before each later retry the wait doubles the previous wait and must never exceed thirty seconds.

judgment.rationale: EV-O-B05 through EV-O-B07 require a two-second first retry wait that doubles on each later retry and is capped at thirty seconds.
